item.title: AI deal frenzy powers Hong Kong fundraising to a record in Jul-Sep
item.description: IPO, placement and block-trade fundraising hits a quarterly record despite stock sell-off and rising bond yields ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: Bankers in Hong Kong skipped the summer break as an AIfueled rush for capital sent share sales to a record, defying abruising selloff in the city’s stocks. Initial public offerings, placements and block trades raised $47.5 billion in JulySeptember, the biggest haul ever for the period, according todata compiled by Bloomberg. That pushed fundraising this year above $92 billion and within reach of the $112.5 billion record set in 2021, though the recent surge in bond yields and poor deal performance are making investors and issuers more cautious. AI has been at the heart of Hong Kong’s deal revival, but this summer brought a new level of intensity.

item.title: How the fashionable Indian was spoilt for choice after 1991 reforms
item.description: Liberalisation brought a flood of international brands into India, but failed to help create a global brand from within the country ...
item.dc:creator: Veenu Sandhu, Sneha Dasghosh
item.content:encoded: India’s affair with the fashion industry started in the colonial era, with the first fashion show, with European clothes and models, held in the 1930s. Post-Independence, after a lull of about a decade, the shows returned in the 1950s with the Spencer sisters — Sylla and Nergish — who brought in the concept of designerwear, choreography and catwalks. That would set the stage for what was to come after India opened itself to the world in 1991.

item.title: Opec+ set to keep November oil output targets steady amid war disruptions
item.description: Gulf Opec+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Opec+ is set to keep oil production targets steady for November, three sources close to the matter said ahead of the group's meeting on Sunday. Gulf Opec+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran, with exports fluctuating at 60-80% of normal levels in recent months. The war has also delayed the group's output capacity review - crucial to determine members' 2027 output quotas - because it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources have said. The Opec+ group, comprising the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia, has agreed in principle to keep targets steady for November, the three sources close to the talks said. Opec+ has been raising output targets for much of 2026 after years of production cuts, but most of the increases stayed on paper because of the Middle East conflict. The seven core Opec+ members pumped 25 million barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly 5 million bpd below prewar levels in February, Opec data shows. Opec+ still has about 2 million bpd of output cuts in place covering most members. It needs a capacity review to decide how to distribute increases and any changes to output are unlikely before 2027, sources have said. The group's seven core members meeting on Sunday are Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman.

item.title: Germany's Merz visits Kyiv as Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian cities
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv Sunday in a show of support as Russia intensifies its attacks on Ukrainian cities.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Germany's Merz visits Kyiv as Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian cities

Germany's Merz visits Kyiv as Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian cities German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv Sunday in a show of support as Russia intensifies its attacks on Ukrainian cities.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz | Photo: Reuters

AP Kyiv 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 04 2026 | 2:29 PM IST

Listen to This Article

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv Sunday in a show of support as Russia intensifies its attacks on Ukrainian cities. The aerial war has intensified, with Moscow menacing cities across Ukraine with hard-to-intercept ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, while Kyiv has been striking Russia's oil industry and businesses. Merz said he travelled to Kyiv, his second trip as chancellor, to demonstrate Germany's support for Ukraine. "If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us," he said in a statement Sunday, adding that he told Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, "You can continue to count on our help."   Merz said the partnership between the two countries was "not a one-way street," pointing to German and Ukrainian companies jointly developing technologies that benefit both sides. "This makes us safer and stronger," he said.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the agenda would focus on "strengthening Ukraine, our defence and resilience, and our shared European security."   Russia's Foreign Ministry said Saturday it would continue to carry out "mass retaliatory strikes" on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, urging foreign nationals and diplomats to leave ?the country. It previously issued a similar warning in May. Also Read

A Russian drone hit Kyiv's Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River again on Sunday morning. Video circulating on social media showed the drone flying into the bridge and the explosion as vehicles crossed. There was no immediate word on casualties. The latest strike came after Russian assaults forced the full or partial closure of three of Kyiv's six road bridges over the Dnipro River earlier this week, suspending traffic and causing tailbacks in Moscow's latest effort to disrupt life in the Ukrainian capital. Previously, Russia has hit apartment blocks, supermarket warehouses, gas stations and data centers, among other targets.

Russia invaded its neighbour more than 4.5 years ago, and there are no concrete signs that a peace settlement might be possible. Fighting along the roughly 1,250-kilometre front line snaking through northern, eastern and southern Ukraine has been virtually deadlocked in recent months.
